name: space-dot-bloom-glides
description: placeDotBloom measured the active dot's offsetLeft while the dot bar was still detached, so --dbx was always written as 0px and the glow under the active space dot never left the left end. Space Run is index 0 and space Empty is index 1 - switching between them has to move the bloom's --dbx to a different value, read straight off the dot bar rather than inferred from a picture.

actions.note: GATE: Run's own tab has committed, so the sidebar and its dot bar exist
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
Run is the active space at launch (index 0) - the bloom's own --dbx, read off the bar rather than off a screenshot
switch to Empty (index 1), the same chord a sibling scenario uses
GATE: the browser committed the switch before the bloom is read again
past the CSS glide the fix relies on

assertions.label: control-the-switch-actually-happened
assertions.desc: CONTROL: without a real switch the two --dbx reads below would just be the same value read twice.

CALIBRATION: the bloom under the centre of Run's dot, measured on a VM run of this fixture's bar. The bloom sits in the dots' own scroller, so this is relative to the scroller's padding edge, 6px of which is clearance for a magnified end dot.
The bloom under Empty's dot moved 14px from dbx-run above - the fix's proof that a switch moves it
